verdict.rationale: Sentry documents an official CLI, and the docs add AI-oriented command-line touchpoints: an `npx @sentry/ai install` command that teaches coding agents to set up Sentry, and an MCP config that reuses the CLI login. However, the CLI's documented primary purpose is debug files, releases and source maps, so AI-native use through the CLI is only thinly evidenced. Missing for 10: documented CLI commands for agent-driven issue triage and querying, structured machine-readable output for agents, and independent or hands-on corroboration of AI-native CLI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: It’s primarily used for managing debug information files for iOS, Android, release and source maps management, as well as code mappings for other platforms.
One command teaches Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Grok how to install and configure Sentry for you.
It uses the CLI login, so the MCP config needs no token.
